Cole, a supervisory law enforcement ranger with the Bureau of Land Management’s Yuma Field Office , was once called into the desert after another hiker found an unconscious woman and called 911. pages.text: Billions of T. rex likely roamed the Earth, paleontologists report | National Geographic Paleontologists figured out how many T. rex lived on Earth—and they found that about 20,000 would have been alive at any given time during a two- to three-million year timespan. Illustration by STOCKTREK IMAGES, Nat Geo Image Collection SCIENCE NEWS Billions of T. rex likely roamed the Earth, paleontologists report The iconic predator’s estimated abundance means the T. rex fossils we have today are exceedingly rare. By Michael Greshko Published April 19, 2021 • 6 min read If you traveled back in time 67 million years ago to ancient Montana, you’d be entering the realm of a tyrant: the iconic predator Tyrannosaurus rex . Before you venture into that lost world, though, you might want to know: On average, how close is the nearest T. rex to you? That might sound like an impossible thing to know—but after crunching through two decades’ worth of T. rex research, a new study provides estimates of the animal’s population density. In all likelihood, a T. rex would be within 15 miles of you, if not much closer. The new study, published last Thursday in Science , also translates these population densities into estimates for how many T. rex ever lived. On average, researchers estimate that some 20,000 T. rex lived at any one time and that about 127,000 generations of the dinosaurs lived and died. Those averages imply that a total of 2.5 billion T. rex lived in the species’ native North America, possibly as far north as Alaska and as far south as Mexico, over a two- to three-million-year timespan.

They are an essential part of American history and embody the strong and resilient characteristics of the American people - so much so that they were designated as our National Mammal in 2016. Once numbering ~30 million and ranging across the United States and in Canada and Mexico, bison were hunted to near extinction, with only several hundred remaining by the 1870’s. Through ongoing conservation work, bison are recovering from a low of fewer than 1,000 individuals. Today, 19 herds in 12 states roam the American Plains. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn BLM Fishing Derby brings Americans Outside for recreation and stewardship in Imperial Valley, California Oct 13, 2026 In a region best known for its off-highway vehicle adventures, the BLM California's El Centro Field Office hooked a different type of recreator for its second annual Fishing Derby Cast and Clean-up event. More than 100 members of the local community gathered for the event on Saturday, Sept. 26, bringing together recreation, community engagement, and public-land stewardship on BLM-managed public lands in Imperial County, California. The fishing derby took place at the Hot Springs Long-Term Visitor Area and on BLM-managed lands adjacent to the Highline and All-American canals. For many attendees, it was their first fishing opportunity, and several first-time anglers caught their first fish. As they fished, participants also collected trash from the surrounding public lands, demonstrating their commitment to responsible recreation and care for the areas they enjoy. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn BLM Turns Wildfire Response into Opportunity for Forest Management and Local Industry Aug 21, 2026 Montrose, Colo. – A firebreak along Cimarron Road during the Gold Mountain Fire served another purpose, too: putting removed trees to use. When wildfire conditions make direct suppression difficult or unsafe, firefighters look for places where they can use the landscape to slow a fire's spread. Reducing vegetation along roads can create a break in fuels, giving firefighters another option if conditions change. That approach was used along nearly 2 miles of Cimarron Road northeast of Ridgway. Crews removed vegetation within approximately 75 feet of the roadside to create a potential firebreak if the fire moved in that direction. Before the work began, Ken Smothers, forester with the BLM's Gunnison Field Office, completed an expedited timber cruise to identify trees that could be recovered and sold rather than left as waste. The District has many challenges to face as it balances its mission of multiple use and sustainable yield to achieve a sustainable ecosystem. Some of the major activities occurring within the district include: livestock grazing, wildland fire suppression, as well as motorized and non-motorized recreation. The Boise District is divided into three geographic areas/field offices: Bruneau (1.4 million acres), Four Rivers (1.3 million acres) and Owyhee (1.2 million acres). The District also manages Idaho's only National Conservation Area, Morley Nelson Snake River Birds of Prey (487,000 acres), home to the greatest concentration of nesting birds of prey in North America – and perhaps, the world. Some 800 pairs of hawks, owls, eagles and falcons come each spring to mate and raise their young here. What are the three branches of government? The Constitution of the United States divides the federal government into three branches: Legislative Judicial Executive This ensures that no individual or group will have too much power. Legislative branch The legislative branch is made up of Congress : The U.S. Senate The U.S. House of Representatives It also includes special agencies and offices that provide support services to Congress. The legislative branch’s key roles include: Drafting proposed laws Confirming or rejecting presidential nominations for heads of federal agencies, federal judges, and the Supreme Court Surveying the budget Having the authority to declare war Judicial branch The judicial branch includes the Supreme Court and other federal courts. It evaluates laws by: Interpreting the meaning of laws Applying laws to individual cases Deciding if laws violate the Constitution Executive branch The president, the vice president, and the president's cabinet are the members of the executive branch. The executive branch’s key roles include: The president is the head of state, leader of the executive branch, and commander in chief of the United States armed forces. The vice president supports the president. If the president is unable to serve, the vice president becomes president. Close BrandonSimons_Aloe's Diary Mapping the Southern African grid from OpenStreetMap, and where the gaps are Posted by BrandonSimons_Aloe on 17 November 2026 in English . I run Aloe Energy, a small not-for-profit initiative working on energy access in Sub-Saharan Africa. We published a free interactive map of the Southern African Power Pool grid, and OpenStreetMap is its backbone, so I wanted to share how it was built and where OSM could use help. What we did. We took every OSM power line of 66 kV and above across the 12 SAPP countries (country extracts from November 2026). Where OSM had no line but an older public map did, we filled the gap from TANESCO (2015) and World Bank (2017) grid maps, but only for lines recorded as existing, with a known voltage, and more than about 3 km from any OSM line. A “Source and age” view on the map colors each line by where it comes from, so you can see exactly what is OSM and what is gap-fill. Where OSM is thin. Coverage is weakest in Tanzania, DR Congo and Angola. Those are the places where the map still leans on maps that are close to ten years old, and where new mapping would change the picture most. Substations named in national plans are often missing too. The map: https://aloeenergy.org/research/sapp-grid . Brìghde Chaimbeul: Tiny Desk Concert October 23, 2026 5:00 AM ET Lars Gotrich Credit: Photo: Vanessa Castilllo/NPR A folk revival only goes so far as an artist's understanding — and adaptation — of tradition. What themes and melodies spoke to the past can easily echo into the present, but come alive through the personality of its interpreter. Brìghde Chaimbeul expands the language of the Scottish smallpipes behind the Desk with a quiet, yet demonstrative presence. Chaimbeul grew up on the Isle of Skye, Scotland, speaking Gaelic and learning the Highland pipes before falling in love with the bellows-blown bagpipe she plays today. Drones are forever with this instrument, but Chaimbeul amplifies, manipulates and darkens the harmonics and frequencies of these pipe drones with effects pedals and contact mics that capture her percussive tapping on the chanter. The effect is mystic and ancient … completely transfixing. Sponsor Message The rhythm of language permeates the songs chosen here — deeply knitting untranslatable wordplay into the drones and melodies. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/11/building-intelligence-first-responders-foundation-models-interoperable UPDATES Building Intelligence for First Responders: From Foundation Models to Interoperable Indoor Data November 5, 2026 Share Facebook Linkedin X.com Email Credit: CTL When a disaster strikes outdoors, first responders are able to capture data from a variety of sources to adequately prepare their response. Satellite imagery, GIS, GPS, and drones all provide the ability to gather information about the scene. However, when a disaster happens indoors, none of those capabilities carry over. The available data becomes 2D, typically a blueprint if it exists, and does not include standpipes, shutoffs, alarm panels, or AEDs. These missing elements are necessary for a safe and timely response by first responders. Without indoor spatial intelligence, responders must make high stakes and high-risk decisions with incomplete information. Fixing the issue requires data that cannot be produced at scale and currently relies on manual documentation. However, many of these structures do not meet current building code requirements and require strategic upgrades. To address this vulnerability, NIST is actively developing best practices, design recommendations, and guidelines for utilizing building retrofit systems to improve the performance of existing structures. Beyond individual structures, it is critical to understand how different retrofit schemes and targets impact the community recovery. NIST is leading ongoing projects to quantify and measure the impact of various retrofit strategies at the community level. By developing the fundamental measurement science needed to assess retrofitted building performance, this work directly supports the long-term resilience and rapid recovery of communities following natural hazards. Since 1995, the CDC Foundation has raised over $2.2 billion and launched more than 1,400 programs impacting a variety of health threats from chronic disease conditions including cardiovascular disease and cancer, to infectious diseases like rotavirus and HIV, to emergency responses, including COVID-19 and Ebola. CDC Launches New Overdose Prevention Data Channel Release For immediate release: August 31, 2026 CDC Media Relations https://www.cdc.gov/media/contact-us/index.html The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) today launched the CDC Overdose Prevention Data Channel , a centralized resource that brings fatal and nonfatal overdose data, prevention strategies, and information about CDC programs together in one place. The launch comes as the latest monthly provisional data from CDC's National Vital Statistics System (NVSS ) predicts 67,798 drug overdose deaths in the United States during the 12 months ending in March 2026. This is a 12.3% decrease in overdose deaths compared to the same time period in the previous year. The continued national decline represents meaningful progress, but too many people still die from drug overdoses. These latest estimates underscore the ongoing need for timely, actionable information to guide overdose prevention efforts.
